problem: The ABAC guard may authorize a request using the shared request organization resolver while messaging and notification services resolve the current organization through a narrower fallback chain. That can make authorization and data access disagree when the tenant is derivable from headers but not attached to the request object.
desired_outcome: Every service-layer path that needs the current organization uses the same resolver as the ABAC guard, so an admitted request and the data path agree on tenant context or fail closed.
requirement_refs: PKMS access control and staff-scoped data isolation

acceptance_criteria.statement: Messaging service organization resolution uses the shared request organization resolver instead of a custom tenant/org/user fallback chain.
Notification service organization resolution uses the shared request organization resolver instead of a custom tenant/org/user fallback chain.
A regression test covers a header-derived tenant path where the ABAC guard and the service layer must resolve the same organization.
The stale user-facing copy 'Organization context is required.' in messaging service error handling is removed or replaced with copy that matches the tenant terminology used by the current codebase.

invariants: PermissionRequired remains the gate for protected GraphQL/admin access.
Services fail closed when no current organization can be resolved.
No cross-tenant fallback to a user's default tenant may override an organization admitted by the request context.
No production secrets, private staff content, or customer data may be logged while diagnosing this path.
non_goals: Do not change the tenant middleware contract unless a blocking defect proves it is necessary.
Do not add new organization or tenant models.
failure_and_rollback_outcome: If remediation fails, leave the existing behavior unchanged and keep the backlog item open. If a merged change causes tenant-resolution regressions, revert the implementation commit and rerun backend tenant and ABAC tests.
